Passes.jl:549 "every other id keeps the entry the pass that closed it wrote, so a closed finding does not reopen for want of a verdict nobody was asked for" — yet :266 `from = ...prevpass..."head"`, :450 `"range" => fixrange`, :611 `elseif entry["act"] == "HONORED" && fav`, and verify-act.js:74 `UNDONE — nothing in the diff addresses this finding.`
verdicts.what_would_bite: The dismissal's own stated ground IS the defect, and it is live and unfixed. Path: `pass_scope` (Passes.jl:263-279) puts a previously-honored id back in scope as a "suspect" whenever a later fix pass touches a file it names (or it names no file at all — then every pass). `pass_open` hands the act verifier only `range = fixrange` = last-graded-pass-head..HEAD (:266, :450), so by verify-act.js:74's own definition the verdict for a fix that landed in an earlier fix range must be UNDONE. `grade` then discards the id's prior entry (only ids OUTSIDE scope are carried, :551-555) and requires `act == "HONORED" && fav` (:611); UNDONE + ABSENT falls through to `closed_by = nothing`, so the id lands in `open_ids` and `close` refuses ("N open id(s) in pass k", :904). Honored re-closure is unreachable for a fix that is demonstrably in the tree — exactly what the record describes for #2 (state ABSENT, act UNDONE at pass-3). The sibling asymmetry is explicit at :549-551: a closed id outside scope is protected from reopening "for want of a verdict nobody was asked for"; a closed id pulled into scope gets no such protection though it is in the same situation. The only exits are an owner ledger entry — which grade counts into `adjudicated_share`, the rate `gbg fleet --diff` compares (Fleet.jl:133) and CHANGELOG's "rates comparable" reports, so machinery artefacts inflate a measured rate — or a carry. The narrowing to `fix_range` was a deliberate cost change (CHANGELOG "The act verifier reads the fix pass's own diff") that never adapted the suspect/regression grading path; verify-act.js has no verdict meaning "still fixed, untouched by this diff". No test asserts the real path: test/rounds.jl:313 is the only suspect case and it hands the suspect a HONORED act verdict ("#2 is a suspect the act verifier re-confirmed") — a verdict the script's own rules forbid when the fix is not in the diff. The substance of #2 is genuinely fixed (close's docstring at Passes.jl:889-893 matches the code's 0/1/2 and the exit-2 branch at :917), so the finding was closed correctly; what was waved through is the grading defect that forced the ledger route, recorded in a dismissal nothing revisits.
